note: Generated by tools/look/build.mjs — see tools/look/README.md. Paths are relative to /look/. Sizes are pixels; tiling_m is the world period in metres that one full texture repeat represents. Height channels are 0 = base, 1 = crest. Normal maps are OpenGL tangent-space (+Y up, +Z toward the viewer).

noise_fine.webp.note: soft cloud noise for the 7/100/500 m fades and for placement jitter; mean 0.5, std 0.13, features 8-16 px; unit tile scaled by the shader

noise_variation.webp.note: patch map (light and dark fields) for the 500/2000 m variation terms; mean 0.5, std 0.12, patches 40-80 px; unit tile scaled by the shader

detail_near.webp.note: multiplicative darkening mask at 100 m: near-white speckle with thin dark squiggles; mean 0.86, std 0.05; unit tile scaled by the shader

detail_far.webp.note: multiplicative darkening mask at 500/2000 m: white with soft grey rock/lichen blotches; mean 0.82, std 0.07; unit tile scaled by the shader

detail_far_winter.webp.note: winter variant of detail_far: whiter, with fine crack and streak structure; mean 0.9, std 0.05; unit tile scaled by the shader

grass.webp.note: neutral grey grass luminance, bright blade tips and dark bases, seamless; desaturated so R=G=B exactly (the shader supplies the green and the dry-peak tints). Height from the Grass004 displacement map.

grass_snow.webp.note: winter grass: nearly white (mean 0.72) with faint dry-stalk structure and soft snow mounds. Height mixes the snow displacement (mounds) with the grass displacement (stalks).

forest_summer.webp.note: brown needle and twig litter with moss patches. Height from the Ground082S displacement blended with Ground023.

forest_spring.webp.note: same litter family as summer with much more moss and fresh green growth over last year needles; clearly greener, not merely brighter. Height from the same displacement blend.

forest_autumn.webp.note: broadleaf litter: dense leaf floor plus whole leaves cut from photo sources and pasted with wrap-around, each with a contact shadow and a darkened rim. Height from the leaf base displacement, raised where a whole leaf lies.

forest_winter.webp.note: frozen and thawed litter: dull grey-brown soil and needles, frost speckle in the hollows, bright (mean 0.58) but not white. Height as summer, with frost filling the lows.

soil.webp.note: bare ploughed earth: matte mid-brown clods. Height from the Ground048 displacement map (clods read in the alpha).

stubble.webp.note: harvested grain field: dry soil with broken straw, short straw stubs standing in rows. All structure comes from photo sources (Ground102 soil, Ground072 straw), nothing drawn. Height from the soil displacement plus the straw ridges.

peat.webp.note: wet dark peat: very dark brown clumps (mean luminance 0.26), a spider-web crack network taken from Ground031, standing water in the lowest spots of the height. Height from the mud luminance blended with the crack displacement.

gravel.webp.note: the verge strip: fine washed grey-brown gravel with a dust matrix, stones 2-10 px. Height from the Gravel003 displacement map.

rock.webp.note: cutting and ravine rock: grey-brown fractured layered rock with moss and dirt in the crevices (moss masked by the displacement lows). Height is the same crack map as rock_height.

rock_height.webp.note: the crack and bump map: white crest, black cracks, std >= 0.18, from the Rock030 displacement map with its large blotches removed. Used as a height-blend weight and a bump input.

sand.webp.note: silt and sand shore: warm grey-ochre with fine ripples, small pebbles cut from Gravel001 where the height is lowest, dark waterline staining in the same lows. Height from the Ground083 displacement.

road_asphalt.webp.note: aged black-grey chip-seal asphalt, polished darker wheel paths at u=0.28/0.72, crown-to-edge grade, two tar-seamed repair patches, one longitudinal crack per wheel path; A=1 over the carriageway, ragged crumb edge whose 0.75 contour sits ~1.4 % in from the mesh edge. v tiles every 24 m, u spans 7 m once

road_overlay_spring.webp.note: fresh moss and young grass creeping in from both edges (pairs of tufts, cut from Grass004 by its blade mask) plus thin moss in the wheel-track cracks; the crown stays clear. Coverage is measured to match the slowroads overlay

road_overlay_autumn.webp.note: fallen birch/aspen/oak leaves: three cut-out species scattered over a litter carpet, densest along both edges and in the wheel tracks, thin on the crown. Warm yellow-ochre-orange-brown aimed at the owner autumn-forest photograph

road_snow.webp.note: pressed bluish-white snow with two polished tyre ruts, grit speckle, patches worn through to wet asphalt and plough crumbs along the edges; A is the same ragged edge mask as the asphalt, so the winter road crumbles into the verge the same way

cell_contents: flowering meadow, 1.25 m (flora mask in cell 3)
layout.uv_per_cell: u = (cell + i) / 8, v = 0 at the cell bottom (base of the plants)
layout.note: greyscale: the game tints each tuft with the same ground colour function it tints the terrain with. Cell world size = the frame the cell was rendered in; render a card of that size (x scale) with the base at v=0.

grass_atlas.webp.note: eight crossed-card tufts, unlit luminance of real 3D plants, cutout in alpha

layout.note: white = flower head (tint with the flower colour of your choice), black elsewhere; same cell layout as grass_atlas.webp

grass_flora.webp.note: mask for the white/yellow flower heads in the flowering-meadow cell

slot_contents: tall roadside herbs (nettle, willowherb) with spring celandine or summer dandelion
juniper / willow scrub (dead branches in winter)
layout.uv_per_slot: u = (slot + i) / 4, v = 0 at the slot bottom (ground contact, sunk 0.18 m)
layout.note: the four slots keep their meaning in every season, so placement never has to change; only the render changes. A bush is 0.3-1.5 m of leaf, always seen against something else, so it keeps photo colour with a per-season grade (spring fresh, summer full, autumn rust, winter dead with snow on the upward faces).
